subject: Question about multistate CMR model in m-array run with JAGS

messages.author: 92ba356136765f03
messages.subject: Question about multistate CMR model in m-array run with JAGS
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to build a multistate model using data summarised in the multistate m-array format (using individual capture histories for my data works but it looks like convergence is weeks or months away for just one model). I have based the code on a CJS CMR model that uses the m-array (from chapter 7 of Kery and Schaub 2012), together with information from Lebreton et al's chapter on multistate CMR in Advances in Ecological Research (2009). A much shortened version of my code, with simulated data is below. The error is the same (just a different index) as my full data set with a more complex model. I've tried all sorts of initial values for phia and psia to no effect.

The code for the state transition matrices is not the most elegant but in testing with defined values appears to do what it's supposed to.

The m-array and probability array are in the format [ release state, recapture state, release year, recapture year ]. Recapture year starts at release year +1.

The final column of the m-array (and corresponding probability array pr.a) is for individuals that were never recaptured. I've added all of these individuals to [ ,1 , , 6 ] because they need to go somewhere. So marray.a[ 2, 1, 3, 6 ] is the total number of individuals released from state 2 at time 3 that were never recaptured. Likewise, pr.a[ 2, 1, 3, 6 ] is the probability that an individual released from state 2 at time 3 was never recaptured.

The model compiles but I keep getting the following error:

Error in jags.model(file = model.file, data = data, inits = inits, n.chains = n.chains,  : 
  Error in node marray.a[1,2,1,1:6]
Node inconsistent with parents


Curiously (to me), even with repeated data simulation and lots of different inits, the error is always at the same node.

Any help would much appreciated as I'm quite stuck. Is this just a problem with inits or could the error signify a more fundamental problem with the model?

N.B. Reposting this as I found a small error in the m-array (index for p in a couple of places; unfortunately the error is still the same).


# Define function to simulate multistate capture-recapture data
simul.ms <- function(PSI.STATE1, PSI.OBS, marked, unobservable = NA){
  # Unobservable: number of state that is unobservable
  n.occasions <- dim(PSI.STATE1)[4] + 1
  CH <- CH.TRUE <- matrix(NA, ncol = n.occasions, nrow = sum(marked))
  # Define a vector with the occasion of marking
  mark.occ <- matrix(0, ncol = dim(PSI.STATE1)[1], nrow = sum(marked))
  g <- colSums(marked)
  for (s in 1:dim(PSI.STATE1)[1]){
    if (g[s]==0) next  # To avoid error message if nothing to replace
    mark.occ[(cumsum(g[1:s])-g[s]+

1)[s]:cumsum(g[1:s])[s],s] <-
      rep(1:n.occasions, marked[1:n.occasions,s])
  } #s
  for (i in 1:sum(marked)){
    for (s in 1:dim(PSI.STATE1)[1]){
      if (mark.occ[i,s]==0) next
      first <- mark.occ[i,s]
      CH[i,first] <- s
      CH.TRUE[i,first] <- s
    } #s
    for (t in (first+1):(n.occasions)){
      # Multinomial trials for state transitions
      if (first>=n.occasions-1) next
      state <- which(rmultinom(1, 1, PSI.STATE1[CH.TRUE[i,t-1],,i,t-1])==1)
      CH.TRUE[i,t] <- state
      # Multinomial trials for observation process
      event <- which(rmultinom(1, 1, PSI.OBS[CH.TRUE[i,t],,i,t-1])==1)
      CH[i,t] <- event
    } #t
  } #i
  # Replace the NA and the highest state number (dead) in the file by 0
  CH[is.na(CH)] <- 0
  CH[CH==dim(PSI.STATE1)[1]] <- 0
  CH[CH==unobservable] <- 0
  id <- numeric(0)
  for (i in 1:dim(CH)[1]){
    z <- min(which(CH[i,]!=0))
    ifelse(z==dim(CH)[2], id <- c(id,i), id <- c(id))
  }
  return(list(CH=CH[-id,], CH.TRUE=CH.TRUE[-id,]))
  # CH: capture histories to be used
  # CH.TRUE: capture histories with perfect observation
}

# 1.2. Generation of simulated data
# Define mean survival, transitions, recapture, as well as number of occasions, states, observations and released individuals
n.occasions <- 6
n.states <- 4
n.obs <- 4
phi.1.a <- 0.8
phi.2.a <- 0.9
phi.3.a <- 0.85
psi12 <- 0.05
psi13 <- 0.02
psi21 <- 0.1
psi23 <- 0.05
psi31 <- 0.05
psi32 <- 0.02
p.1 <- 1  # starting p for each colony is the same
p.2 <- 1
p.3 <- 1
# modifiers for p at each recapture occasion (length = occ - 1)
rp1<- runif(n.occasions-1, 0.4,0.7)
rp2 <- runif(n.occasions-1, 0.4,0.7)
rp3 <- runif(n.occasions-1, 0.4,0.7)
marked <- matrix(NA, ncol = n.states, nrow = n.occasions)
marked[,1] <- rep(50, n.occasions)    # Site 1
marked[,2] <- rep(50, n.occasions)    # Site 2
marked[,3] <- rep(50, n.occasions)    # Site 3
marked[,4] <- rep(0, n.occasions)    # Dead individuals

# Define matrices with survival, transition and recapture probabilities
# These are 4-dimensional matrices, with
# Dimension 1: state of departure
# Dimension 2: state of arrival
# Dimension 3: individual
# Dimension 4: time
# 1. State process matrix
totrel <- sum(marked)*(n.occasions-1)
PSI.STATE1 <- array(NA, dim=c(n.states, n.states, totrel, n.occasions-1))
for (i in 1:totrel){
  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    PSI.STATE1[,,i,t] <- matrix(c(
      phi.1.a*(1-(psi12+psi13)), phi.1.a*psi12, phi.1.a*psi13,     1-phi.1.a,
      phi.2.a*psi21, phi.2.a*(1-(psi21+psi23)), phi.2.a*psi23,     1-phi.2.a,
      phi.3.a*psi31, phi.3.a*psi32,    phi.3.a*(1-(psi31+psi32)),  1-phi.3.a,
      0,           0,              0,                        1        ), nrow = n.states, byrow = TRUE)
  } #t
} #i
# 2.Observation process matrix
PSI.OBS <- array(NA, dim=c(n.states, n.obs, totrel, n.occasions-1))
for (i in 1:totrel){
  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    PSI.OBS[,,i,t] <- matrix(c(
      p.1*rp1[t], 0, 0, 1-(p.1*rp1[t]),
      0, p.2*rp2[t], 0, 1-(p.2*rp2[t]),
      0, 0, p.3*rp3[t], 1-(p.3*rp3[t]),
      0, 0, 0, 1    ), nrow = n.states, byrow = TRUE)
  } #t
} #i

# Execute simulation function
sim <- simul.ms(PSI.STATE1, PSI.OBS, marked)
CH1 <- sim$CH

# Compute vector with occasion of first capture
get.first <- function(x) min(which(x!=0))
f <- apply(CH1, 1, get.first)

# Function to create a multistate m-array based on capture-histories (CH) when no recaptures
marraymulti.N <- function(CH,states){
  nind <- dim(CH)[1]
  n.occasions <- dim(CH)[2]
  m.array <- array(data = 0, dim = c(states,states,n.occasions,n.occasions+1))
  get.first.1.N <- function(x) min(which(x==1))
  get.first.2.N <- function(x) min(which(x==2))
  get.first.3.N <- function(x) min(which(x==3))
  pos1 <- apply(CH,1,get.first.1.N)
  remove1 <- which(pos1=="Inf")
  pos1 <- pos1[-remove1]
  pos2 <- apply(CH,1,get.first.2.N)
  remove2 <- which(pos2=="Inf")
  pos2 <- pos2[-remove2]
  pos3 <- apply(CH,1,get.first.3.N)
  remove3 <- which(pos3=="Inf")
  pos3 <- pos3[-remove3]
  g1 <- length(pos1)
  g2 <- length(pos2)
  g3 <- length(pos3)
  for (z in 1:g1){
    m.array[1,1,pos1[z],dim(m.array)[4]] <- m.array[1,1,pos1[z],dim(m.array)[4]] + 1
  } #z
  for (z in 1:g2){
    m.array[2,1,pos2[z],dim(m.array)[4]] <- m.array[1,1,pos2[z],dim(m.array)[4]] + 1
  } #z
  for (z in 1:g3){
    m.array[3,1,pos3[z],dim(m.array)[4]] <- m.array[1,1,pos3[z],dim(m.array)[4]] + 1
  } #z
  out <- m.array[,,1:(n.occasions-1),2:(n.occasions+1)]
  return(out)
}

# Function to create a multistate m-array based on capture-histories (CH) with at least 1 recapture
marraymulti.R <- function(CH,states){
  nind <- dim(CH)[1]
  n.occasions <- dim(CH)[2]
  m.array <- array(data = 0, dim = c(states,states,n.occasions,n.occasions+1))
 
  # The following gives pairs of positions and pairs of states for release-recapture when at least 1 recapture
  pos_all <- array((0),dim=c(1,2))
  statepairs_all <- array((0),dim=c(1,2))
  for (i in 1:dim(CH)[1]){
    pos <- which(CH[i,]!=0)
    pospairs <- cbind(pos[-length(pos)],pos[-1])
    CH_s <- CH[i,! CH[i,] %in% 0]
    statepairs <- cbind(CH_s[-length(CH_s)],CH_s[-1])
    pos_all <- rbind(pospairs,pos_all)
    statepairs_all <- rbind(statepairs,statepairs_all)
  } #i
 
  state_pos <- cbind(statepairs_all,pos_all)
 
  state1_1 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==1 & state_pos[,2]==1),],ncol=4)
  state1_2 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==1 & state_pos[,2]==2),],ncol=4)
  state1_3 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==1 & state_pos[,2]==3),],ncol=4)
  state2_1 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==2 & state_pos[,2]==1),],ncol=4)
  state2_2 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==2 & state_pos[,2]==2),],ncol=4)
  state2_3 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==2 & state_pos[,2]==3),],ncol=4)
  state3_1 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==3 & state_pos[,2]==1),],ncol=4)
  state3_2 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==3 & state_pos[,2]==2),],ncol=4)
  state3_3 <- matrix(state_pos[(state_pos[,1]==3 & state_pos[,2]==3),],ncol=4)
  state1_1 <- matrix(state1_1[,3:4],ncol=2)
  state1_2 <- matrix(state1_2[,3:4],ncol=2)
  state1_3 <- matrix(state1_3[,3:4],ncol=2)
  state2_1 <- matrix(state2_1[,3:4],ncol=2)
  state2_2 <- matrix(state2_2[,3:4],ncol=2)
  state2_3 <- matrix(state2_3[,3:4],ncol=2)
  state3_1 <- matrix(state3_1[,3:4],ncol=2)
  state3_2 <- matrix(state3_2[,3:4],ncol=2)
  state3_3 <- matrix(state3_3[,3:4],ncol=2)
 
 
  for (i in 1:dim(state1_1)[1]){
    m.array[1,1,state1_1[i,1],state1_1[i,2]] <- m.array[1,1,state1_1[i,1],state1_1[i,2]] + 1
  }
  for (i in 1:dim(state1_2)[1]){
    m.array[1,2,state1_2[i,1],state1_2[i,2]] <- m.array[1,2,state1_2[i,1],state1_2[i,2]] + 1
  }
  for (i in 1:dim(state1_3)[1]){
    m.array[1,3,state1_3[i,1],state1_3[i,2]] <- m.array[1,3,state1_3[i,1],state1_3[i,2]] + 1
  }
  for (i in 1:dim(state2_1)[1]){
    m.array[2,1,state2_1[i,1],state2_1[i,2]] <- m.array[2,1,state2_1[i,1],state2_1[i,2]] + 1
  }
  for (i in 1:dim(state2_2)[1]){
    m.array[2,2,state2_2[i,1],state2_2[i,2]] <- m.array[2,2,state2_2[i,1],state2_2[i,2]] + 1
  }
  for (i in 1:dim(state2_3)[1]){
    m.array[2,3,state2_3[i,1],state2_3[i,2]] <- m.array[2,3,state2_3[i,1],state2_3[i,2]] + 1
  }
  for (i in 1:dim(state3_1)[1]){
    m.array[3,1,state3_1[i,1],state3_1[i,2]] <- m.array[3,1,state3_1[i,1],state3_1[i,2]] + 1
  }
  for (i in 1:dim(state3_2)[1]){
    m.array[3,2,state3_2[i,1],state3_2[i,2]] <- m.array[3,2,state3_2[i,1],state3_2[i,2]] + 1
  }
  for (i in 1:dim(state3_3)[1]){
    m.array[3,3,state3_3[i,1],state3_3[i,2]] <- m.array[3,3,state3_3[i,1],state3_3[i,2]] + 1
  }
 
  out <- m.array[,,1:(n.occasions-1),2:(n.occasions+1)]
  return(out)
}

# Adults
# Create adults m-array
CH.A.m <- CH1
CH.A.R_or_N <- CH.A.m
CH.A.R_or_N[CH.A.R_or_N==2] <- 1
CH.A.R_or_N[CH.A.R_or_N==3] <- 1
CH.A.R_or_N[CH.A.R_or_N==4] <- 1
cap <- apply(CH.A.R_or_N, 1, sum) # vector of each individual with number of total captures incl release
ind <- which(cap >= 2)  # vector of IDs of indivs recaptured at least once
CH.A.R <- CH.A.m[ind,]    # Adult CH recaptured at least once
CH.A.N <- CH.A.m[-ind,]   # Adult CH never recaptured
CH.A.R.marray <- marraymulti.R(CH.A.R,3)
CH.A.N.marray <- marraymulti.N(CH.A.N,3)
# Add adults never recaptured m-array to adults recaptured m-array
CH.A.marray <- CH.A.R.marray + CH.A.N.marray

#----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RUN THE MODEL
#----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#-------------------------------------------------
# Load required package
#-------------------------------------------------
library(rjags)
library(jagsUI)

# Specify model in BUGS language
sink("ipm_ms_marray_sim.txt")
cat("
    var pr.a[3,3,5,6];
    model {
    #----------------------------------------
    # 1. Define the priors for the parameters
    #----------------------------------------
   
    #-------------------------
    # 2. Parameters time-dependent
    #-------------------------
    for (i in 1:3) {  # states
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    phia[i,t] ~ dunif(0, 1)  # Adult apparent survival
    }
    }
    for (i in 1:3) {  # states
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    p3[1,i,t] ~ dunif(0, 1)    # Recapture probability as 3+yo (adult)
    p3[2,i,t] <- p3[1,i,t]
    p3[3,i,t] <- p3[1,i,t]
    }
    }
   
    # Transitions: multinomial logit
    # Normal priors on logit of all but one transition probas
    for (i in 1:3){
    for (j in 1:2){
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    lpsia[i,j,t] ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
    } #t
    } #j
    } #i
    # Constrain the transitions such that their sum is < 1
    for (i in 1:3){  # departure state
    for (j in 1:2){  # arrival state
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    psia[i,j,t] <- exp(lpsia[i,j,t]) / (1 + exp(lpsia[i,1,t]) + exp(lpsia[i,2,t]))
    } #u
    } #i
    } #t
   
    # Calculate the last transition probability
    for (i in 1:3){
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    psia[i,3,t] <- 1-psia[i,1,t]-psia[i,2,t]
    } #u
    } #t
   
    for (i in 1:3){
    for (j in 1:3){
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    T_a[i,j,t] <- phia[i,t]*psia[i,j,t]
    }
    }
    }
   
    #--------------------------------------------
    # 4. The likelihoods of the single data sets
    #--------------------------------------------
   
    # 4.2 Likelihood for capture-recapture data: Multistate model (3 states and 3 age classes)
    # Multinomial likelihood
    for (i in 1:3){
    for (j in 1:3){
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    marray.a[i,j,t,1:nyears] ~ dmulti(pr.a[i,j,t,], r.a[i,t])
    }
    }
    }
   
    # Adults
    pr.a[,,1,1] <- (T_a[,,1]*p3[,,1])
    pr.a[,,1,2] <- ((T_a[,,1]*(1-p3[,,1])) %*% (T_a[,,2]*p3[,,2]))
    pr.a[,,1,3] <- ((T_a[,,1]*(1-p3[,,1])) %*% (T_a[,,2]*(1-p3[,,2])) %*% (T_a[,,3]*p3[,,3]))
    pr.a[,,1,4] <- ((T_a[,,1]*(1-p3[,,1])) %*% (T_a[,,2]*(1-p3[,,2])) %*% (T_a[,,3]*(1-p3[,,3])) %*% (T_a[,,4]*p3[,,4]))
    pr.a[,,1,5] <- ((T_a[,,1]*(1-p3[,,1])) %*% (T_a[,,2]*(1-p3[,,2])) %*% (T_a[,,3]*(1-p3[,,3])) %*% (T_a[,,4]*(1-p3[,,4])) %*% (T_a[,,5]*p3[,,5]))

    pr.a[,,2,2] <- ((T_a[,,2]*p3[,,2]))
    pr.a[,,2,3] <- ((T_a[,,2]*(1-p3[,,2])) %*% (T_a[,,3]*p3[,,3]))
    pr.a[,,2,4] <- ((T_a[,,2]*(1-p3[,,2])) %*% (T_a[,,3]*(1-p3[,,3])) %*% (T_a[,,4]*p3[,,4]))
    pr.a[,,2,5] <- ((T_a[,,2]*(1-p3[,,2])) %*% (T_a[,,3]*(1-p3[,,3])) %*% (T_a[,,4]*(1-p3[,,4])) %*% (T_a[,,5]*p3[,,5]))

    pr.a[,,3,3] <- ((T_a[,,3]*p3[,,3]))
    pr.a[,,3,4] <- ((T_a[,,3]*(1-p3[,,3])) %*% (T_a[,,4]*p3[,,4]))
    pr.a[,,3,5] <- ((T_a[,,3]*(1-p3[,,3])) %*% (T_a[,,4]*(1-p3[,,4])) %*% (T_a[,,5]*p3[,,5]))

    pr.a[,,4,4] <- ((T_a[,,4]*p3[,,4]))
    pr.a[,,4,5] <- ((T_a[,,4]*(1-p3[,,4])) %*% (T_a[,,5]*p3[,,5]))

    pr.a[,,5,5] <- ((T_a[,,5]*p3[,,5]))

    # Below main diagonal
    for (i in 1:3){
    for (j in 1:3){
    for (r in 2:(nyears-1)){
    for (t in 1:(r-1)){
    pr.a[i,j,r,t] <- 0   
    }
    }
    }
    }
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    # Last column
    pr.a[1,1,t,nyears] <- 1-sum(pr.a[1,,t,1:(nyears-1)])
    pr.a[2,1,t,nyears] <- 1-sum(pr.a[2,,t,1:(nyears-1)])
    pr.a[3,1,t,nyears] <- 1-sum(pr.a[3,,t,1:(nyears-1)])
    for (i in 1:3){
    for (j in 2:3){
    pr.a[i,j,t,nyears] <- 0
    }
    }
    } #t
   
    }
    ",fill = TRUE)
sink()


# Bundle data

# Row sums to get number of each age class released from each state per year
nyears <- 6
r.j <- r.s <- r.a <- matrix((0),nrow=3,ncol=10)
for (i in 1:3){
  for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
    r.a[i,t] <- sum(CH.A.marray[i,,t,])
  }
}
jags.data <- list(nyears = nyears, marray.a = CH.A.marray, r.a = r.a
)

# FUNCTIONS

init.phia <- function(lower,upper){
  phi.array <- array((0),dim=c(3,nyears-1))
  for (i in 1:3){
    for (j in 1:(nyears-1)){
      phi.array[i,j] <- runif(1,lower,upper)
    }
  }
  return(phi.array)
}

# Temp array for p
init.p <- function(miss_yr){  # miss_yr = year that age group not seen
  p.array <- array((0),dim=c(3,3,nyears-1))
  for (i in 1:3){
    for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
      p.array[1:3,i,t] <- runif(1,0.3,0.5)
    }}
  for (i in 1:3){
    p.array[1:3,i,miss_yr] <- NA # recap years in which age not seen (1 for sub, 1:2 for ad)
  }
 
  return(p.array)
}

# Function to create initial values for psi age/col
init.psi <- function(cols){
  psi.array <- array(NA,dim=c(cols,cols-1,nyears-1))
  for (i in 1:cols){
    for (j in 1:(cols-1)){
      for (t in 1:(nyears-1)){
        psi.array[i,j,t] <- rnorm(1)
      } #t
    } #j
  } #i

  return(psi.array)
}


# Initial values
inits <- function(){list(phia = init.phia(0.5, 0.9),
                         p3 = init.p(NA),
                         lpsia = init.psi(3)
)}

# Parameters monitored
params <- c("phia", "psia", "p3"
)

# Test MCMC settings
ni <- 10000
nt <- 5
nb <- 5000
nc <- 2
ncores <- 2

# Call JAGS from R
start.time = Sys.time()
out.sim <- jags(jags.data,
                 inits=inits,
                 parameters.to.save=params,
                 model.file="ipm_ms_marray_sim.txt",
                 n.chains = nc,
                 n.thin = nt,
                 n.iter = ni,
                 n.burnin = nb,
                 parallel = FALSE,
                 n.cores = ncores,
                 DIC=FALSE)
end.time = Sys.time()
elapsed.time = difftime(end.time, start.time, units='mins')
cat("Sample analyzed after ", elapsed.time, ' minutes\n')

messages.subject: Re: Question about multistate CMR model in m-array run with JAGS
parts:
I've just experimented with the m-array by moving the totals for never recaptured in each year from [ , 1 , , 6] to [ , 2 , , 6 ] and the error is now at node marray.a[1,2,1,1:6]
It looks like the problem is in how I've put the total number of individuals never recaptured in only a single recapture state. I've only done that because they're associated with the release state only and I need to be able to sum across release state to get total numbers released for each state for dmulti(). I wondered if this could be an issue when I first thought about how to convert the CJS m-array to multistate m-array. I can't think of a way around it so I'm pretty stumped.

messages.author: 92ba356136765f03
messages.subject: Re: Question about multistate CMR model in m-array run with JAGS
parts: OK, I've figured it out. The problem was indeed the empty "final columns" for individuals never recaptured. To resolve it I've stacked the recapture arrays next to each other for each release state, giving a single column at the end for individuals never recaptured, for each release state. Most of the code is the same as the original post, just with a few index changes and code to reformat the recapture array and probability array from four dimensions to three. It's just run successfully (and much quicker than the state space formulation with individual capture histories).
